title: The birth of Islam
description: In 622, a merchant from Mecca named Muhammad fled his city for Medina. That departure, the Hijra, marks year 1 of Islam and the start of a world civilization.
subject: histoire

title: Urban II's call and the First Crusade
description: In November 1095, at Clermont, Pope Urban II made a call that sent tens of thousands of Europeans toward Jerusalem. The Crusades were born.
subject: histoire

title: The sack of Rome by the Visigoths
description: In August 410, Alaric's Visigoths looted Rome for three days. For the first time in eight centuries, an enemy army walked into the Eternal City.
subject: histoire

title: The coronation of Charlemagne
description: On Christmas Day 800, in Rome, Pope Leo III placed a crown on Charlemagne's head. The West had an emperor again, and Europe had a model that would last.
subject: histoire

title: Magna Carta
description: In June 1215, John Lackland set his seal to a charter forced on him by his barons. Over the centuries, a feudal text became the symbol of law standing above the king.
subject: histoire

title: The Black Death in Europe
description: Between 1347 and 1353, bubonic plague killed 30 to 60% of Europeans. A health catastrophe that shook medieval society and sped up the shift into a new world.
subject: histoire

title: Joan of Arc and the Hundred Years' War
description: In 1429, a 17-year-old peasant girl persuaded the Dauphin to hand her an army. Within months, Joan of Arc turned around a war France seemed to have lost.
subject: histoire

title: The Fall of Constantinople
description: On May 29, 1453, after 53 days of siege, the Ottomans forced the walls of Constantinople. The New Rome fell, and the Middle Ages tipped into a new age.
subject: histoire

title: The Aztec Empire
description: In less than two centuries, the Aztecs built a capital of 200,000 people on a lake. Their empire, founded on tribute and sacrifice, collapsed in two years once the Spanish arrived.
subject: histoire

title: The discovery of America
description: On October 12, 1492, Christopher Columbus reached an island in the Bahamas that he believed was Japan. One navigational error opened the age of globalization.
subject: histoire

title: The storming of the Bastille
description: On July 14, 1789, a Paris crowd stormed a fortress that held only **7 prisoners**. That act became the symbol of the French Revolution.
subject: histoire

title: Napoleon's strategy at Ulm
description: In October 1805, Napoleon surrounded and captured **60,000 Austrians** in two weeks, with almost no major battle. Ulm showed the power of speed.
subject: histoire

title: The Battle of Waterloo
description: On **June 18, 1815**, in a single rainy day in Belgium, Napoleon's empire collapsed. Waterloo closed the Hundred Days and opened a century of monarchical order in Europe.
subject: histoire

title: The Paris Commune
description: From March 18 to May 28, 1871, Paris governed itself for **72 days**. The experiment ended in the Bloody Week, a crackdown that left a lasting mark on French memory.
subject: histoire

title: The Belle Époque
description: Between the end of the war of 1870 and August 1914, Europe believed in progress. Electricity, world's fairs, brand-new art movements, and the cracks that led to catastrophe.
subject: histoire

title: The Battle of Verdun
description: For **299 days**, French and German armies tore each other apart around Verdun. **700,000** casualties for almost no ground gained: the symbol of the horror of the trenches.
subject: histoire

title: The Russian Revolution
description: In less than eight months, Russia went from the rule of the tsars to the rule of the Bolsheviks. 1917 invented a model that would divide the world for decades.
subject: histoire

title: The Great Depression
description: On **October 24, 1929**, Wall Street collapses. Within three years **25%** of Americans are out of work, and the crisis opens the way for political extremism in Europe.
subject: histoire

title: The Battle of Stalingrad
description: From the summer of 1942 to February 1943, Germans and Soviets killed each other in the ruins of a city on the Volga. Stalingrad became the turning point of the Second World War.
subject: histoire

title: Hiroshima and Nagasaki
description: On **August 6, 1945**, an atomic bomb flattened Hiroshima. Three days later, Nagasaki. The Second World War ended, and the nuclear age began.
subject: histoire

title: Rosa Parks and Montgomery
description: On **December 1, 1955**, a seamstress refused to give up her seat on a bus in Montgomery. Her arrest launched a **381-day** boycott and changed the civil rights movement.
subject: histoire

title: The Cuban Missile Crisis
description: In October **1962**, the world spent **13 days** a hair away from nuclear war. Missiles in Cuba, fleets on alert: the Cold War reached its peak.
subject: histoire

title: The Algerian War
description: For **eight years**, France fought a war of independence on land it insisted was its own. The Algerian War brought down the Fourth Republic and left lasting scars.
subject: histoire

title: The Battle of Dien Bien Phu
description: From **March 13** to **May 7, 1954**, a French army besieged in a valley in northern Vietnam surrendered to the Viet Minh. The defeat ended French Indochina.
subject: histoire

title: The Armenian Genocide
description: Between **1915** and **1916**, the Ottoman government organized the deportation and systematic killing of much of the empire's Armenian population.
subject: histoire

title: The creation of the UN
description: On **June 26, 1945**, **51** countries signed the Charter of the United Nations in San Francisco. Born from the ashes of the Second World War, the UN set out to spare the world the scourge of war.
subject: histoire

title: The birth of the EU
description: The European Union grew out of one practical idea: make war between France and Germany physically impossible by tying together coal and steel. Small steps led from **1950** to Maastricht.
subject: histoire

title: The Rwandan genocide
description: In **100 days**, between April and July **1994**, hundreds of thousands of Tutsis and moderate Hutus were killed in Rwanda. The fastest genocide of the century unfolded in full view of the world.
subject: histoire

title: The fall of the Berlin Wall
description: On the night of **November 9 to 10, 1989**, Berliners tore down with their bare hands the wall that had divided their city for **28 years**. A misunderstanding on live television sped up the end of the Cold War.
subject: histoire

title: Blitzkrieg
description: In **six weeks**, from **May 10** to **June 22, 1940**, the German army conquered France and the Benelux countries. This “lightning war” rewrote the art of war through sheer speed.
subject: histoire

title: The Marshall Plan
description: In **1947** Europe lay in ruins. The United States offered massive aid to rebuild it, and to hold back communism.
subject: histoire

title: The Vietnam War
description: For twenty years the United States poured enormous force into Vietnam to hold back communism. It got bogged down, tore itself apart, and left without winning.
subject: histoire

title: The Nuremberg trials
description: Between **1945** and **1946**, **24** Nazi leaders stood trial at Nuremberg. For the first time, an international court invented crimes against humanity.
subject: histoire

title: Decolonization: an overview
description: Between **1945** and **1975**, more than **80** countries won their independence. The European empires collapsed and the map of the world changed.
subject: histoire

title: Apartheid and Mandela
description: For **46** years South Africa organized racial segregation by law. **Nelson Mandela**, after **27** years in prison, helped the country leave it behind without a civil war.
subject: histoire

title: The Cultural Revolution in China
description: Between **1966** and **1976**, **Mao Zedong** launched a purge of extreme violence to take power back. Red Guards, chaos, then the pragmatic turn of **Deng Xiaoping**.
subject: histoire

title: The Holocaust: the mechanics of a genocide
description: Between **1941** and **1945**, the Nazi regime organized the murder of six million Jews. The Holocaust was not a sudden burst of hatred. It was a process run by a state.
subject: histoire

title: September 11, 2001
description: On **September 11, 2001**, nineteen Al-Qaeda terrorists hijacked four planes. The deadliest attack in American history opened the era of the war on terror.
subject: histoire

title: Athenian democracy
description: In the 5th century BC, Athens invented a system where citizens governed directly. Selection by lot, an equal right to speak, and exclusion on a massive scale.
subject: histoire

title: The American Civil War
description: From **1861** to **1865**, the United States tore itself apart: more than **620,000** dead. At the heart of the war, slavery, national unity, and the birth of a stronger federal state.
subject: histoire

title: Why is the sky blue?
description: Looking at a blue sky is so ordinary that we forget to ask why. The answer lies in the light of the Sun and in the air we look through to see it.
subject: sciences

title: Why do we dream?
description: Every night you dream for about two hours. Most of those dreams are gone the moment you wake. Here is what science understands about the mystery today.
subject: sciences

title: Why does ice float?
description: Ice floats on water. It looks perfectly normal, but it is in fact very rare. And lucky for life on Earth.
subject: sciences

title: Why is seawater salty?
description: A liter of seawater holds about 35 grams of salt. That salt has been building up for billions of years. Here is where it comes from.
subject: sciences

title: Why are there seasons?
description: The seasons do not come from Earth being closer to or farther from the Sun. The real cause is the tilt of Earth's axis.
subject: sciences

title: How do planes fly?
description: A plane weighing several hundred tons flies. It is not magic: it comes down to the shape of a wing, speed, and forces that balance out.
subject: sciences

title: Why do we yawn?
description: Everyone yawns: humans, dogs, sometimes even unborn babies. It is probably not about running short of oxygen. Here are the strongest leads.
subject: sciences

title: How does memory work?
description: Memory is not a camera. Every recollection is rebuilt. Here is how the brain encodes, stores, and sometimes invents.
subject: sciences

title: Why do we get chills?
description: Cold, fear, music: chills have several causes. They all run through the nervous system, but not for the same reasons.
subject: sciences

title: How does soap kill viruses?
description: Soap is not magic. It attacks the fatty shell of certain viruses and pulls them off your skin. Here is why 20 seconds matter.
subject: sciences

title: The discovery of penicillin
description: In 1928, Alexander Fleming noticed that a mold had killed the bacteria on a culture dish. That accident produced the first great antibiotic.
subject: sciences

title: The discovery of electricity
description: Electricity was not invented in one stroke. It was first observed, then understood, then tamed. Here are the key steps.
subject: sciences

title: The discovery of X-rays
description: In 1895, Wilhelm Röntgen discovered an invisible radiation that passes straight through matter. Within months, medicine saw a revolution in it.
subject: sciences

title: The discovery of the microwave oven
description: In 1945, an engineer noticed that the chocolate bar in his pocket had melted next to a radar set. That observation gave us the microwave oven.
subject: sciences

title: The theory of gravitation
description: In 1687, Newton published a simple and enormous idea: the same force makes an apple fall and keeps the Moon in its orbit. Here is what it changed.
subject: sciences

title: The discovery of radioactivity
description: With Pierre Curie and Henri Becquerel, Marie Curie opened the chapter of radioactivity. Two Nobel Prizes, a crushing workload, and an immense legacy.
subject: sciences

title: The invention of the Internet
description: The Internet has no single inventor. It is a long chain: a military network, a common language, then the Web for human beings.
subject: sciences

title: The structure of DNA
description: In 1953, Watson and Crick described the double helix of DNA. Behind that glory stands the crucial work of Rosalind Franklin.
subject: sciences

title: The discovery of anesthesia
description: Before 1846, patients were often awake and in extreme pain while surgeons worked. Anesthesia turned an operation into treatment instead of torture.
subject: sciences

title: Darwin's theory of evolution
description: In 1859, Darwin published On the Origin of Species. The core idea: living things change over time through natural selection.
subject: sciences

title: The Big Bang
description: 13.8 billion years ago, the universe started to expand. This is not a bomb going off in a void: space itself is what grows.
subject: sciences

title: Why do volcanoes erupt?
description: A volcano is an opening in the Earth's crust. Magma under pressure rises through it and becomes lava. Here is why the Earth “spits.”
subject: sciences

title: How do earthquakes happen?
description: Every year the Earth records hundreds of thousands of earthquakes. Most go unnoticed. A few change whole cities.
subject: sciences

title: The Chernobyl disaster (1986)
description: On April 26, 1986, reactor No. 4 at Chernobyl exploded. It is the worst civil nuclear accident in history. Here is what happened, without the sensationalism.
subject: sciences

title: Why doesn't the Moon fall to Earth?
description: The Moon is falling toward the Earth all the time. It simply misses, every single time. That is exactly what an orbit is.
subject: sciences

title: Is there life elsewhere in the Universe?
description: Trillions of planets, and yet total radio silence. Science looks for life elsewhere without promising little green men.
subject: sciences

title: What is a black hole?
description: A black hole is not a cosmic vacuum cleaner. It is a region where gravity is so strong that not even light can escape.
subject: sciences

title: The theory of relativity for everyone
description: In 1905 and 1915, Einstein changed our idea of space, time and gravity. And without his calculations, your GPS would be off by several kilometers.
subject: sciences

title: How does lightning form?
description: Lightning is not magic: it is an enormous electrical discharge inside a storm cloud. Here is how it builds up, and then how it strikes.
subject: sciences

title: What is the greenhouse effect (really)?
description: The greenhouse effect is not a problem in itself: it is the invisible blanket that keeps the Earth from freezing. The real trouble starts when we thicken it too fast.
subject: sciences

title: Why do we sleep?
description: We spend a third of our lives asleep. It is not wasted time: sleep cleans the brain, repairs the body and etches memories into place.
subject: sciences

title: How does the brain store memories?
description: Memory is not a library of drawers. It is a living network of neurons that strengthen, rebuild themselves and sometimes get it wrong.
subject: sciences

title: Why are some species immortal?
description: Some species seem to defy death. Jellyfish that grow young again, hydras that never age: the secret is cell repair.
subject: sciences

title: Photosynthesis explained simply
description: Plants do something extraordinary: they cook sugar out of light, water, and air. And they hand us the oxygen as a gift.
subject: sciences

title: Why do leaves change color?
description: Autumn does not invent the colors. It removes the green that was hiding them. Behind the show sits a survival plan for getting through winter.
subject: sciences

title: What is dark matter?
description: No one has ever seen it. Yet without it, galaxies would come apart. Dark matter is the invisible glue of the universe.
subject: sciences

title: How does electricity work in our body?
description: Thinking, a heartbeat, lifting an arm: all of it travels first as living electricity, carried not by electrons but by ions.
subject: sciences

title: Why do some sounds give us chills?
description: Goosebumps, tingles, a racing heart: music can hijack the circuits we use for pleasure and for survival. Here is why.
subject: sciences

title: Why do other planets have seasons?
description: On Earth, the seasons come from the tilt of the axis. Elsewhere the same rule gives winters that last 42 years, or almost no seasons at all.
subject: sciences

title: The Odyssey, Homer
description: After Troy, Odysseus, king of Ithaca, takes ten years to get home. Monsters, gods and temptations mark out a voyage that invents the cunning hero of Western literature.
subject: litterature

title: The Iliad, Homer
description: Not the whole Trojan War: 51 days of wrath. Achilles withdraws, Patroclus dies, Hector falls. Homer shows how glory can turn brutal, then human again.
subject: litterature

title: Oedipus Rex, Sophocles
description: Oedipus wants to save Thebes from a plague. As he investigates, he discovers that he is the guilty man. Sophocles invents the tragedy in which knowing means destroying yourself.
subject: litterature

title: Antigone, Sophocles
description: Antigone buries her brother against the order of King Creon. Between the law of the city and duty to family, Sophocles sets up a conflict that has never aged.
subject: litterature

title: The Symposium, Plato
description: Around an Athenian dinner, the guests take turns defining love. Aristophanes tells the story of the androgynes, Socrates lifts desire toward the Beautiful. Plato turns a party into philosophy.
subject: litterature

title: The Republic, Plato
description: To define justice, Plato imagines an ideal city and the myth of the cave. The Republic is not an election platform: it is an inquiry into the soul and into power.
subject: litterature

title: The Apology of Socrates, Plato
description: In 399 BC, Athens put Socrates on trial. Accused of corrupting the young, he refused to plead for pity. Plato fixed the founding scene of Western philosophy.
subject: litterature

title: The Poetics, Aristotle
description: Aristotle analyzes Greek tragedy and coins words that are still everywhere: mimesis, catharsis, peripeteia. The Poetics is the first great instruction manual for storytelling.
subject: litterature

title: Works and Days, Hesiod
description: Hesiod speaks to his brother Perses: work, be just, beware of excess. Between the myth of Pandora and a farming calendar, an ethic of labor is born.
subject: litterature

title: Medea, Euripides
description: Jason leaves Medea for a princess. She kills their children. Euripides creates a heroine who is terrifying, brilliant and foreign: passion turns into reasoning.
subject: litterature

title: Les Misérables, Victor Hugo
description: Jean Valjean looks for redemption in a France that refuses to forgive him. Hugo mixes love story, historical chronicle and a plea for the outcast.
subject: litterature

title: Madame Bovary, Flaubert
description: Emma Bovary confuses real life with the romantic novels she has read. Flaubert invents the modern novel, and the trial that makes it famous.
subject: litterature

title: The Red and the Black, Stendhal
description: Julien Sorel, a carpenter's son, wants to rise in a France that is closed to him. Stendhal invents the modern psychological novel.
subject: litterature

title: Candide, Voltaire
description: Candide crosses a cruel world still believing that all is for the best. Voltaire demolishes the optimism of Leibniz with relentless irony.
subject: litterature

title: The Confessions, Rousseau
description: Rousseau tells his own life with an honesty nobody had risked before. The Confessions invent modern autobiography and open the way to Romanticism.
subject: litterature

title: The Stranger, Camus
description: Meursault does not cry at his mother's funeral. In 123 pages of stripped-down prose, Camus invents the absurd.
subject: litterature

title: The Myth of Sisyphus, Camus
description: Camus starts from suicide in order to define the absurd. Sisyphus, condemned to roll a rock forever, becomes the hero of a clear-eyed joy.
subject: litterature

title: In Search of Lost Time, Proust
description: Seven volumes, 1.5 million words: Proust explores involuntary memory and makes time the main character of the novel.
subject: litterature

title: Père Goriot, Balzac
description: Goriot gives up everything for two ungrateful daughters. Rastignac learns Paris at the expense of an old man and a convict. Balzac invents The Human Comedy.
subject: litterature

title: Les Fleurs du Mal, Baudelaire
description: Baudelaire draws beauty out of evil and out of everyday life in Paris. Condemned in 1857, Les Fleurs du Mal founded modern poetry.
subject: litterature

title: 1984, George Orwell
description: Published in 1949, 1984 invented Big Brother, Newspeak, and the Ministry of Truth. Orwell describes a society where surveillance and state lies grind down the individual until he loves the tyrant.
subject: litterature

title: Animal Farm, George Orwell
description: In 1945, Orwell tells the story of a farm where the animals drive out the farmer, then watch the pigs take his place. A crystal-clear allegory of the Russian Revolution and of a revolution betrayed.
subject: litterature

title: Hamlet, Shakespeare
description: Around 1601, Shakespeare wrote Hamlet, a prince who hesitates after his father's murder. Between revenge, feigned madness, and the question “To be or not to be,” the modern hero of conscience is born.
subject: litterature

title: Romeo and Juliet, Shakespeare
description: Around 1595, two lovers in Verona die in less than five days. Shakespeare compresses a romance into a social tragedy: clan hatred destroys the young.
subject: litterature

title: Brave New World, Aldous Huxley
description: In 1932, Huxley imagined a happy, stable future where people give up freedom for pleasure. Soma, genetic castes, and endless entertainment: the other great dystopia of the 20th century.
subject: litterature

title: Frankenstein, Mary Shelley
description: In 1818, an 18-year-old Mary Shelley wrote the first great science-fiction novel. Victor Frankenstein creates life, then runs from his creature: a fable about science without ethics.
subject: litterature

title: Crime and Punishment, Dostoyevsky
description: In 1866, Raskolnikov kills a pawnbroker to prove that he is a superman. Dostoyevsky turns the crime into a laboratory of conscience and redemption.
subject: litterature

title: The Trial, Kafka
description: Josef K. is arrested one morning without being told why. Kafka describes an endless trial and an opaque bureaucracy: the word “Kafkaesque” was born from this nightmare.
subject: litterature

title: Don Quixote, Cervantes
description: Don Quixote charges at windmills, convinced he is fighting giants. Cervantes invents the modern novel out of generous madness, irony, and metafiction.
subject: litterature

title: The Grapes of Wrath, Steinbeck
description: In 1939, the Joad family leaves a drought-stricken Oklahoma behind. Steinbeck tells the story of the Okie exodus and celebrates a solidarity that stands up to injustice.
subject: litterature

title: To Kill a Mockingbird, Harper Lee
description: Scout, six years old, watches the town of Maycomb, Alabama. Between children's games and an unjust trial, Harper Lee shows moral courage facing down racism.
subject: litterature

title: The Great Gatsby, Fitzgerald
description: Jay Gatsby throws lavish parties to win Daisy back. Fitzgerald paints the Jazz Age and the corruption of the American dream.
subject: litterature

title: The Lord of the Rings, Tolkien
description: Frodo must destroy the One Ring in Mount Doom. Tolkien invents Middle-earth and redefines modern fantasy.
subject: litterature

title: Fahrenheit 451, Bradbury
description: In this future, firemen burn books. Guy Montag discovers that culture dies of indifference as much as of censorship.
subject: litterature

title: One Hundred Years of Solitude, García Márquez
description: Seven generations of Buendías in Macondo. García Márquez blends wonders and tragedy to tell the history of Latin America.
subject: litterature

title: The Metamorphosis, Kafka
description: Gregor Samsa wakes up turned into an insect. Kafka shows how a family, and a whole society, reject the person who can no longer work.
subject: litterature

title: The Master and Margarita, Bulgakov
description: The devil visits Stalin's Moscow while a writer tells the story of Pontius Pilate. Bulgakov's answer to censorship: manuscripts do not burn.
subject: litterature

title: Moby-Dick, Melville
description: Ishmael signs on to the Pequod to hunt Moby Dick. Melville mixes sea adventure, the science of whales, and a meditation on obsession.
subject: litterature

title: The Little Prince, Saint-Exupéry
description: A little prince from a tiny planet teaches a stranded pilot that what really matters is invisible to the eye.
subject: litterature

title: The Alchemist, Paulo Coelho
description: Santiago, an Andalusian shepherd, sets out for the Pyramids to find a treasure. Coelho turned the search for self into a worldwide phenomenon.
subject: litterature

title: The Italian Renaissance
description: In two centuries, Italy reinvented painting, sculpture, and architecture, and changed the way we see the world.
subject: art

title: The birth of Impressionism
description: In 1874, painters rejected by the Salon put on their own show. A critic mocked Monet and accidentally gave **Impressionism** its name.
subject: art

title: Caravaggio and chiaroscuro
description: **Michelangelo Merisi**, known as Caravaggio, changed painting forever with brutal realism and an extreme contrast of light and shadow: chiaroscuro.
subject: art

title: Rembrandt and the Flemish school
description: **Rembrandt van Rijn** was the great painter of the Dutch Golden Age. Self-portraits, biblical scenes, and *The Night Watch*: he painted the human soul.
subject: art

title: Romanticism in painting (Delacroix, Géricault)
description: Between 1810 and 1850, Romanticism revolted against the coldness of Neoclassicism. Color against line, passion against reason: **Géricault** and **Delacroix**.
subject: art

title: Cubism: Picasso and Braque
description: Between 1907 and 1920, **Picasso** and **Braque** broke the object into facets seen from several angles at once. The most radical revolution since the Renaissance.
subject: art

title: Surrealism: Dalí and Magritte
description: Born in 1924, Surrealism set out to free the unconscious: dreams, desires, wild associations. **Dalí** raves, **Magritte** puzzles.
subject: art

title: Expressionism: Munch and The Scream
description: Expressionism puts inner feeling ahead of the outside world. With **Munch** and *The Scream*, modern dread became an icon.
subject: art

title: Abstract art: Kandinsky and Mondrian
description: For the first time, a painting represented nothing at all from the visible world. **Kandinsky** set forms free; **Mondrian** cut everything down to geometry.
subject: art

title: Pop Art: Warhol and Lichtenstein
description: Pop Art answers the consumer society head-on. **Warhol** and **Lichtenstein** turn advertising, comic books and movie stars into high art.
subject: art

title: The birth of electronic music
description: From the theremin to the clubs of Chicago and Detroit, electronic music invents sounds without an orchestra and changes the way the world dances.
subject: art

title: Bob Dylan and protest folk
description: From Greenwich Village to the Nobel Prize, Bob Dylan turns folk song into political poetry, then into electric rock.
subject: art

title: Hip-hop: the birth of a culture
description: Born in the Bronx in 1973, hip-hop invents the DJ, rap, breakdancing and graffiti, then conquers the planet.
subject: art

title: Verdi's operas
description: Giuseppe Verdi turns Italian opera into a political weapon and a theater of the soul: Rigoletto, La Traviata, Aida, Otello.
subject: art

title: Mozart: child prodigy, tragic life
description: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, an early genius from Salzburg to Vienna, invents the independent composer and leaves an unfinished Requiem.
subject: art

title: Beethoven: genius and deafness
description: Ludwig van Beethoven, from Bonn to Vienna, composes his greatest works as he goes deaf and invents the romantic genius.
subject: art

title: The birth of rock'n'roll
description: In the mid-1950s, Black blues and white country merge: Elvis, Chuck Berry and Little Richard invent rock'n'roll.
subject: art

title: Bach and Baroque music
description: Johann Sebastian Bach, cantor at Leipzig, pushed the fugue and counterpoint to their highest point and became the architect of the Baroque.
subject: art

title: The birth of American jazz
description: Born in New Orleans, jazz blended African rhythms, the blues, and European harmony, then invented swing, bebop, and modal jazz.
subject: art

title: The blues: roots of all modern music
description: Born in the cotton fields of Mississippi, the blues invented the 12-bar grid and fed jazz, rock, soul, and hip-hop.
subject: art

title: The birth of photography
description: In **1839**, several inventors finally worked out how to fix an image on a plate. In less than a century, photography changed the way we see, remember, and believe.
subject: art

title: Charlie Chaplin and silent cinema
description: **Charlie Chaplin** invented the Tramp, a vagrant in a bowler hat, and became the first global movie star. From silent film to sound, he turned laughter into an art.
subject: art

title: Orson Welles and Citizen Kane
description: At **25**, **Orson Welles** directed *Citizen Kane* (**1941**). The film invented a new language: deep focus, flashbacks, and a hunt for one mysterious word, Rosebud.
subject: art

title: The French New Wave
description: Young critics at *Cahiers du cinéma* stepped behind the camera. Between **1959** and **1968**, the New Wave freed film from the studio and invented modern auteur cinema.
subject: art

title: Kubrick and 2001: A Space Odyssey
description: In **1968**, **Stanley Kubrick** turned science fiction into a sensory experience. Few lines of dialogue, exact images, and one question: what becomes of humans when they face their own tools?
subject: art

title: Hitchcock and suspense
description: **Alfred Hitchcock** invented modern suspense: give the audience information the characters do not have. In *Psycho*, *Vertigo* and *Rear Window*, he plays with where we look.
subject: art

title: Gothic architecture: the cathedrals
description: From the 12th to the 16th century, Gothic cathedrals pushed stone toward the sky. Pointed arches, rib vaults, stained glass: a technical revolution in the service of light.
subject: art

title: The Bauhaus
description: Between **1919** and **1933**, the **Bauhaus** school fused art, craft and industry in Germany. Closed by the Nazis, it still spread modern design across the world.
subject: art

title: The Mona Lisa
description: Painted by **Leonardo da Vinci** between **1503** and **1519**, the *Mona Lisa* became the absolute icon of the Louvre. Technique, a mysterious smile, and a theft in **1911** that changed everything.
subject: art

title: The Starry Night, Van Gogh
description: In **1889**, from the asylum at Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, **Vincent Van Gogh** painted *The Starry Night*. The sky swirls: art stops copying the real world and starts speaking an emotion.
subject: art

title: Guernica, Picasso
description: After the bombing of Guernica, Picasso painted a black-and-white scream against war. The canvas traveled the world, then came home to Spain once Franco was gone.
subject: art

title: Liberty Leading the People, Delacroix
description: Delacroix painted the Three Glorious Days of July 1830: Marianne holding the flag, a mixed crowd, barricades. Political Romanticism walked into the museum.
subject: art

title: The Creation of Adam, Michelangelo
description: On the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel, Michelangelo painted God and Adam with their fingers almost touching. A masterpiece of fresco and of the Cinquecento.
subject: art

title: Impression, Sunrise, Monet
description: A seascape of Le Havre painted at speed, a mocking critic, and the word “impressionism” was born. Monet caught one bright, industrial moment.

title: Nighthawks, Hopper
description: In a New York diner, Hopper painted American urban loneliness. Nighthawks became the icon of a country brightly lit and completely alone.

title: Les Demoiselles d'Avignon, Picasso
description: Five nudes built from facets and masks: Les Demoiselles d'Avignon breaks with imitation and opens the door to Cubism. Even Picasso's friends were scandalized.

title: The Persistence of Memory, Dalí
description: Soft watches on the Catalan coast: Dalí painted time melting. A surrealist icon that ended up at MoMA and in pop culture.

title: Greek tragedy and ancient theater
description: In Athens, Aeschylus, Sophocles, and Euripides invented tragedy. Chorus, hubris, catharsis: a theater built for thinking about the city.

title: Shakespeare's theater
description: In London, Shakespeare wrote for the Globe. Hamlet, Macbeth, Romeo: popular theater that became the high point of the English language.

title: Press freedom and photojournalism
description: From Cartier-Bresson to Nick Ut, news photography pins history down in a single image. Freedom, ethics, and media power in the same viewfinder.

title: The birth of the Greek gods
description: Before Zeus, his father Cronus devoured his own children. Here is how the void gave birth to the gods of Olympus.

title: Prometheus, the fire thief
description: Prometheus stole fire from the gods and gave it to humans, then endured an endless torture. A myth about progress, cunning, and the price of freedom.

title: Pandora and the box
description: The first woman made by the gods, Pandora opened a jar full of plagues. Hope stayed at the bottom. A myth about curiosity and misfortune.

title: Demeter and Persephone
description: Hades carries Persephone off. Her mother Demeter, goddess of the harvest, lets the earth starve. A myth built to explain the seasons.

title: Orpheus and Eurydice
description: Orpheus goes down to the underworld to bring Eurydice back. His music bends death itself. One forbidden glance is enough to lose everything.
subject: mythologie

title: Narcissus and Echo
description: Echo can only repeat. Narcissus loves nothing but his reflection. Two fates that never manage to meet, and that gave us the word narcissism.
subject: mythologie

title: Icarus and Daedalus
description: Daedalus builds wings of wax to escape Crete. His son Icarus flies too high, falls, and gives his name to a sea. A myth about measure and excess.
subject: mythologie

title: Sisyphus: eternal punishment
description: Sisyphus cheats Death, then the gods themselves. His sentence: roll a rock that always falls back. Camus turned him into the symbol of clear sight in the face of the absurd.
subject: mythologie

title: Tantalus and his torment
description: Tantalus serves his own son to the gods. His sentence: water and fruit forever out of reach. A myth of frustration that even named a chemical element.
subject: mythologie

title: Medusa and Perseus
description: Medusa turns anyone who looks at her to stone. Perseus beats her with a mirrored shield, then saves Andromeda. The head of the Gorgon becomes a protective symbol.

title: Hercules and his 12 labors
description: Heracles, son of Zeus, kills his own family in a fit of madness. His Twelve Labors are a penance: kill monsters, then defeat death itself.
subject: mythologie

title: Theseus and the Minotaur
description: Theseus kills the Minotaur thanks to Ariadne's thread. But he forgets to change the sails: his father Aegeus throws himself into the sea, which still carries his name.
subject: mythologie

title: Odysseus and the Cyclops
description: In the Odyssey, Odysseus faces the Cyclops Polyphemus. His [[metis]] saves him, but his pride draws down the anger of Poseidon.
subject: mythologie

title: Odysseus and the Sirens
description: The Sirens promise absolute knowledge. Odysseus is the only mortal who hears their song and lives, thanks to a trick that became a model of self-control.
subject: mythologie

title: Jason and the Golden Fleece
description: Jason and the Argonauts sail to Colchis to bring back the Golden Fleece. Behind the adventure lies a story of love and betrayal with the sorceress Medea.
subject: mythologie

title: Achilles: the heel and invulnerability
description: Achilles, the hero of the Iliad, looks unbeatable. One heel, one arrow, and the myth invents the universal metaphor for a fatal weak point.

title: Oedipus and the Sphinx
description: Oedipus saves Thebes by solving the riddle of the Sphinx. Yet this victory of the mind opens the door to the most terrible tragedy of all.

title: Antigone: family duty versus the law of the state

title: The Trojan War and the wooden horse

title: Thor and Loki (Norse mythology)

title: Ragnarök: the end of the Norse world

title: Osiris and Set (Egyptian mythology)

title: Gilgamesh: the first hero in history

title: Romulus and Remus: the founding of Rome

title: Vishnu and Shiva (Hindu mythology)

title: The Valkyries and Valhalla

title: Merlin the Enchanter
